newsitem.title: USA: Miami Heat star Tim Hardaway cited for speeding.
newsitem.headline: Miami Heat star Tim Hardaway cited for speeding.

text.p: Basketball star Tim Hardaway was cited for speeding after he was caught doing 70 mph (112 kph) over the speed limit in a construction zone near Miami Beach's trendy model mecca South Beach, police said on Monday.

Hardaway, a National Basketball Association all-star who led the Miami Heat to the Eastern Conference championship last season, was ticketed on Friday for driving his blue Ferrari at 110 mph (176 kph) in a 40 mph (64 kph) zone across a causeway linking Miami Beach and Miami, according to a police report.

The Ferrari, bearing the vanity plate "THARD," and another car, a Porsche, were chased along the causeway by Miami Beach police who said they were unable to catch Hardaway until traffic forced them to slow down. The other car got away.
As the officers were writing Hardaway a ticket, he "became hostile and militant," suggesting that he was stopped because "he was black and he was a Miami Heat player," the police report said.
Police said Hardaway was not arrested but could be fined up to $515 because he was cited for speeding in a construction zone.
Hardaway's Heat lost the conference final to the Chicago Bulls, who went on to win the league championship.
